# Preface {.unnumbered}

QViz is an educational visualiser for trapped-ion quantum circuits. A Qiskit
circuit and a chosen backend are turned into a JSON file. That file describes
the native ion gates and the state of every qubit after every gate. A web page
then draws the ions as Bloch spheres.

The purpose is **pedagogical**. There is a gap between the logical gates of a
circuit and the native gates that the machine really runs. By showing every
native gate and the state of every ion, the gap is closed, and the physics of
each gate can be explained. See [Why QViz](docs/concepts/motivation.qmd).

This book documents the whole project. Its main subject is the **backend**
(Python), which is described module by module. It also covers how the parts are
connected, the **viewer** that draws the JSON, and its use on Qollab.

The book is written in plain English. Short sentences and the passive voice are
used, so that the reader is not required to be an expert. Every public function
is described, together with its parameters, its return value and its units.

The pages are grouped as follows.

- **Introduction** explains why the project exists.
- **Getting started** shows how the project is installed and run.
- **Core concepts** explains the pipeline, the units and the JSON contract.
- **Architecture** shows how the library, the adapters, the viewer and the hosts
  are connected, how the repository is organised and which engineering practices
  are followed.
- **Backend modules** documents each module, function by function.
- **Examples** shows complete circuits, such as the QFT adder.
- **Frontend** documents the architecture of the viewer, the viewer itself and its
  use on Qollab.
- **Development** explains the tests, the demo scripts, the style rules and the
  tooling and workflow.

The complete rendered book can be built with Quarto. See
[Installation](docs/getting-started/installation.qmd) for the
commands.
